card.name: Small words after a complete clause
card.fires_on: Short linking words such as "in", "on", or "apparently" that come right after a finished statement about an event or symptom. A qualifier phrase such as "in addition", "in patients without", or "in the absence of" usually follows.

modes.label: "in" after an event
modes.description: The word "in" follows a reported event or reaction and introduces who it occurred in or what was absent.
modes.example: of age. DIES is a non-IgE mediated hypersensitivity reaction characterized by protracted vomiting occurring 1 to 4 hours after drug ingestion<< in>> the absence of skin or respiratory symptoms.

modes.label: "on" after appear
modes.description: The word "on" follows "appear" and introduces where something shows up.

card.writes: It promotes "otherwise" and similar words, which suggests the model expects a contrast or condition clause next.
card.plain: It fires on a small linking word right after a statement, where a condition or contrast like "in the absence of" or "in patients without" tends to follow.
